title: Convolution second-moment bound
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\\varphi$ be a probability density on $(\\mathbb F_2)^n$, let $F:(\\mathbb F_2)^n\\to\\mathbb R$ satisfy $|F(x)|=1$ for every $x$, and let $\\varepsilon\\in\\mathbb R$. Suppose every nonzero binary frequency $\\gamma$ satisfies $|\\widehat\\varphi(\\gamma)|\\le\\varepsilon$. Then $\\mathbb E_x(\\varphi*F)(x)^2\\le (\\mathbb E_xF(x))^2+\\varepsilon^2$, with uniform averages and normalized convolution on the cube.
hypotheses_covered: $\\varphi$ is a pointwise nonnegative function on $(\\mathbb F_2)^n$ with uniform average $1$
all nonzero-frequency Fourier coefficients of $\\varphi$ have absolute value at most $\\varepsilon$
